## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Nirodhavāra* (Ya 6.2.2) is a subsection of the *Yamaka*, the sixth book of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka. Structurally, the chapters of the *Yamaka* regularly divide their procedural or process sections (*pavattivāra*) into three operational modes: origination (*uppādavāra*), cessation (*nirodhavāra*), and combined origination-and-cessation (*uppādanirodhavāra*) [Gal 2003; Ronkin 2005]. Through a rigorous matrix of paired questions and categorical distributions, the *nirodhavāra* investigates the temporal dynamics of how particular phenomena cease in relation to persons and realms [Gal 2003; Ronkin 2005]. Scholarly analysis observes that this formal examination reflects an early Buddhist process metaphysics and marks a critical milestone in the development of the Abhidhamma theory of momentariness, utilizing the technical division of a moment (*khaṇa*) into phases of origination and dissolution (*uppādakkhaṇa*, *bhaṅgakkhaṇa*) [Gal 2003; Ronkin 2005].
